name: Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma Type 2

criteria.description: Presence of multiple discrete, hyperkeratotic, spiny papules on the palms and soles
Histological evidence of focal hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis and absence of epidermolytic changes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in AAGAB gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological confirmation; genetic testing and family history supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may aid confirmation.

laboratory: Histopathology showing focal hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis without epidermolytic changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in AAGAB gene identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Lesions tend to be larger and more diffuse
Presence of cornoid lamella on histology
Lesions often have an atrophic center with raised border
May have risk of malignant transformation

redFlags: Rapid increase in lesion size or number
Development of ulceration or bleeding within lesions
Signs of secondary infection such as increased pain, erythema, or purulence
